review_scope: Bounded revision of computational provenance, curve/event conventions, and a new length-64 replacement experiment. The complete Section 30 proof chain and the recent flatness preprint are not audited by this increment.
path_convention: Local paths are relative to the research repository root; historical output remains distinct from replacement output.

status_definitions.derivation_checked: A local identity or finite-computation convention was checked by derivation; this does not classify all proofs in the chapter.
status_definitions.external_statement_checked: The named local statement was checked against the cited primary source, without re-refereeing the full source.
status_definitions.exact_finite_check: Exact rational or algebraic arithmetic verifies the named finite inputs or identities, not transcendental values.
status_definitions.numerical_check: Recorded comparisons for a bounded run, with precision and tolerance; no interval certificate or asymptotic consequence.
status_definitions.conditional_bound: An exact finite implication given an explicit error hypothesis that the computation does not certify.
status_definitions.reported_unreplayed: Historical values are retained with their provenance; the purported original raw evidence is unavailable and the claim has not been replayed.
status_definitions.outside_increment_review: Text is preserved; this computational revision does not establish its general proof or source status.

claims.scope: Signed primitive-vector counts, normalized shortest nonzero lattice vector, strict convexity hypotheses. The new unoriented torus counts do not verify the general discrepancy argument.
External rational-polygon theorems and their lack of transfer to strictly convex norm balls remain distinct from this experiment.

hypotheses: N(L)/L^2 tends to a fixed c.
The series is the limit of telescoping partial sums; absolute convergence needs the displayed growth conditions.
claims.scope: Finite iteration leaves the remainder 4^(-k)E(2^k L), which tends to zero. A bounded finite computation cannot infer an O(L) or o(L) remainder.

hypotheses: A block [T,2T] requires the complete spectrum through 4T.

The inverse-width proof, local profile models, exact primitive-row formula, and geometric hypotheses are preserved. The trace experiment does not identify a supporting rational normal at an irrational flat point.

claims.scope: Primitive slopes modulo sign correspond to unoriented essential simple curves. The edge identity is tr(A)tr(B)=tr(AB)+tr(AB^-1). Distinct slopes are not deduplicated by trace.
Exact Q(sqrt(11)) arithmetic verifies x^2+y^2+z^2=xyz and the reduced-root inequalities. Exact traces do not imply exact lengths.

hypotheses: These two reduced fixtures have minimum root trace at least 5/2.
The positive outward subtraction ratio is at most one half.
claims.scope: v=log(trace/2) grows at least additively with the sector weight F. Since v>=F/5 and length>2v, length<=64 implies max(|p|,q)<160. This gives an analytic finite-box bound; membership decisions within the box use numerical transcendental comparisons.

New length-64 experiment: 1104 modular and 1127 asymmetric curves; blocks T=4,8,16 only. Binary64 log traversal and independent primitive-slope box evaluation agree. Decimal lengths at 100/140 digits agree within the declared tolerance. M/Q event sweeps are compared against direct counts on every interval.
claims.coverage_gap: No reproduction of length8192, no long twist-path campaign, no certified event locations or ordering, and no asymptotic conclusion. Log-vs-oracle metric discrepancies are retained as diagnostics.
